We just let that message reappear in the queue and then SQS eventually will retry again.
Other types of errors can be fatal errors that are maybe bugs in the code or things that really need to be looked at by a member of our team.

So, we have a group of applications called the Creep Keeper.
The Creep Keeper takes care of our dead messages.
So, there's an application that consumes these messages from the dead letter queue and saves them into a database called the MorkDB.
And we also have another application which is a web interface called the Morktician that gives our team members the ability to see what's going on in this database.
Take a look at the messages, see how many messages are in the MorkDB.
And we can also, with another application called Lazarus, which revives these dead messages, can send them back to the appropriate queues.
